# Use output-hygiene

<!-- Generated by build_pack_guides.py from pack.json and the skills' own files. Edit those, not this. -->

Review agent-written text before it ships and strip the machine artifacts it carries — invisible Unicode, non-breaking spaces, homoglyphs, harness-added provenance trailers, trailing chat closers — then flag the prose tells a script cannot catch, each quoted with a rewrite.

**Reach for it when** the user wants to clean up AI-generated output, asks to remove a Claude watermark, attribution footer, or "Generated with" line, wants a draft that does not read as machine-written, or needs a pre-ship hygiene pass on a document, commit message, or pasted chat answer.

## Install it

```bash
npx skilldrop-cli install output-hygiene                 # Claude Code, your user folder
npx skilldrop-cli install output-hygiene --project       # Claude Code, this repo
npx skilldrop-cli install output-hygiene --ide cursor    # or kiro, codex, antigravity, copilot
```

It is part of the Core pack: [`--pack core`](../packs/use-the-core-pack.md) installs it with its neighbours.

It ships scripts, so it needs Python 3 (standard library only, nothing to install). What they may touch is declared in [its manifest](../../../packs/core/skills/output-hygiene/manifest.json).

## Ask for it

Say it the way you would to a colleague. Requests like these route to it:

- "Remove the Claude watermark from this doc before I send it"
- "Strip the 'Generated with Claude Code' footer and the co-author trailer"
- "This draft sounds like AI — tell me exactly which sentences give it away"
- "There are invisible characters in this file breaking my diff, find them"
- "Clean up this text I pasted out of a chat window before it goes to the board"

Requests like these belong to a different skill, so it shouldn't answer them:

- "Review this design doc and tell me where the argument is weak"
- "Summarize this report for executives"
- "Write our company policy on acceptable AI use"

If another skill answers instead, ask for this one by name: "use output-hygiene".

## Check what you get

A good result:

- **Every mechanical finding names a codepoint or quotes the matched line.** "Contains invisible characters" is unverifiable; `3:18 U+00A0 NO-BREAK SPACE` is checkable in one keystroke.
- **Every prose finding quotes the span it is judging.** The quote is the evidence. A finding that paraphrases is an opinion.
- **The auto and review tiers stay separate in the report.** Merging them means the user approves a homoglyph guess while approving a zero-width-space deletion.
- **The medium is stated before the first finding.** Half the classes are medium-dependent; a report that skips it is asserting a default it never disclosed.
- **Rewrites are paste-able.** "Tighten this" is not a rewrite. The replacement sentence is.
- **The report says what it left alone.** Including the provenance trailer when disclosure is owed, and why.

## Use something else when

- The document's argument, structure, or evidence is the problem — that is `doc-critique`.
- The goal is to pass work off as unassisted where a policy requires disclosure. The skill stops on the provenance class and names the policy.
- The text is source code. Invisible-character scanning is worth running, but prose tells do not apply and the rewrite advice will be wrong.
- The user wants the text shortened or re-pitched for a different audience. That is a rewrite, not a hygiene pass.

## Where a loop runs it

- Stage `confirm` of the [`apply` loop](../../../packs/career/loops/apply/LOOP.md), where gate G6.1 decides
- Stage `polish` of the [`ship-a-draft` loop](../../../packs/core/loops/ship-a-draft/LOOP.md)
